title: ICE agents could soon use gloves that give painful electric shocks
excerpt: The devices are already in use by law enforcement agencies across the U.S.
content_html:
U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers could soon use gloves that can give a painful electric shock to anyone they touch. 

As first reported by the Associated Press, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) published a notice on Monday revealing plans to distribute electrically powered shock gloves to ICE agents by the end of March next year. Called the G.L.O.V.E. (an acronym for Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter), the device is developed by Kentucky company Compliant Technologies, which markets it as a "Conductive Distraction and De-escalation Device" or CD3. 

"CD3s are not weapons — they deliver small, non-injurious electrical pulses directly to the surface of the skin, the body’s largest and most conductive organ, achieving NPI (Neuro Peripheral Interference)," Compliant Technologies states on its website. In short, the gloves cause a painful electric shock.

You May Also Like

According to Compliant Technologies, the G.L.O.V.E "delivers a pain stimulus strictly to the area" of the skin that it touches, overstimulating and disrupting signals in the nervous system. This overwhelms and overloads the brain, causing a person to instinctively attempt to retreat.

"Because the effect is so intense, it disrupts normal thought processes and interferes with expected reactions," the company states. "In most cases, this results in the subject effectively complying or conceding in order to end the effects."

G.L.O.V.E. devices will be supplied to officers and agents across ICE's Homeland Security Investigations and Enforcement Removal Operations divisions, with the DHS's notice stating that it plans to spend up to $20 million to purchase them. The DHS is specifically interested in the CTG-5 G.L.O.V.E. model, which can output around 324-362 volts (to a maximum of 380) at 700-1200mA by touching a person. In comparison, Axon Enterprise's TASER 10 delivers under 1000 volts at 1.5mA via prongs that pierce the skin.

Higher voltage better enables electricity to flow through obstacles such as air, clothes, or flesh, while amplitude measures the strength of the current. As such, amplitude determines an electrical shock's physical impact, though voltage affects the force at which electricity is actually delivered. The G.L.O.V.E's low voltage means it will only work when directly applied to bare skin (or through thin clothing that is soaked).

Though designed to be non-lethal, the G.L.O.V.E. does have risks. Compliant Technologies' user manual warns that applying more than two G.L.O.V.E devices to a single individual "may result in injury or death," and recommends that it be used for no longer than 15 seconds. It also cautions against using the G.L.O.V.E. on vulnerable demographics such as small children or elderly people, or grabbing a person's head, face, throat, chest, or groin.

Mashable Light Speed

"In our opinion, Compliant Technologies' CD3 technology is the safest, most humane, common-sense, de-escalatory technology ever introduced into public service," Compliant Technologies' website states.

Mashable reached out to Compliant Technologies, which declined to comment further.

In a statement to Mashable, a DHS spokesperson said that ICE officers are "highly trained in de-escalation tactics," and that they relieve regular ongoing training regarding use of force.

"ICE is constantly assessing the needs of our officers in the field to ensure they have the tools and equipment necessary to safely arrest and remove criminal illegal aliens from our country,: said the DHS spokesperson. "Every decision is made with careful consideration and appropriately reviewed to ensure that any technology ICE utilizes is consistent with all applicable law enforcement policies and standards."

However, human rights advocates have crticised the rollout of the G.L.O.V.E to ICE agents. ICE has received significant attention for its agents' use of force, which many voters feel is excessive.

"ICE has betrayed the public's faith and at this point cannot be trusted to use force on American streets, let alone to use an untested technology against anyone they perceive as a threat," Naureen Shah, the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU)'s director of government affairs, Equality Division, said in a statement to Mashable.

Multiple U.S. agencies already use the G.L.O.V.E

Credit: Compliance Technologies

ICE is far from the first U.S. government agency to use the G.L.O.V.E., which has been around since 2018. Compliant Technologies' exclusive dealer APB Consulting Solutions claims that over 700 U.S. local law enforcement agencies use CD3 technology, and that it is the largest dealer of such devices in the country.

The Cape Girardeau Police Department in Missouri started using the G.L.O.V.E after reportedly learning about it in 2022, while Louisville Metro Department of Corrections was among around 50 Kentucky agencies using the device that year. The Harris County Sheriff's Office in Texas has a policy in place for use of the G.L.O.V.E., the Johnson County Sheriff's Office in Missouri shared a video of officers training to use it last year, and Compliant Technologies announced in July that it had won a contract with the North Carolina Sheriff's Association.

Kentucky's Bullitt County Detention Center previously used the G.L.O.V.E. as well, but ceased in 2023 after an employee was found to have used excessive force when applying one to a handcuffed and shackled inmate.

UPDATE: Aug. 14, 2026, 10:20 a.m. AEST This article has been updated with comment from the DHS and ACLU.

content_html_zh:
美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）官员很快就会使用手套，这种手套可能会给他们接触到的任何人带来痛苦的电击。

据美联社首次报道，美国国土安全部 (DHS) 周一发布通知，计划在明年 3 月底之前向 ICE 特工分发电动防震手套。 称为 G.L.O.V.E. （生成低输出电压发射器的缩写），该设备由肯塔基州 Compliant Technologies 公司开发，该公司将其作为“传导分散和降级设备”或 CD3 进行销售。

Compliant Technologies 在其网站上表示：“CD3 不是武器，它们直接向皮肤表面（人体最大、导电性最强的器官）传递微小、无害的电脉冲，从而实现 NPI（神经外周干扰）。” 简而言之，手套会导致痛苦的电击。

你可能也喜欢

根据 Compliant Technologies 的说法，G.L.O.V.E 会“严格向其接触的皮肤区域传递疼痛刺激”，从而过度刺激和扰乱神经系统中的信号。 这会使大脑不堪重负，导致人本能地试图撤退。

该公司表示：“由于效果如此强烈，它会扰乱正常的思维过程并干扰预期的反应。” “在大多数情况下，这会导致对象有效地服从或让步，以结束效果。”

手套。 这些设备将提供给 ICE 国土安全调查和执法遣返行动部门的官员和特工，国土安全部的通知称，计划斥资高达 2000 万美元购买这些设备。 DHS 对 CTG-5 G.L.O.V.E 特别感兴趣。 模型，通过触摸人可以输出约 324-362 伏（最大 380）、700-1200mA 电流。 相比之下，Axon Enterprise 的 TASER 10 通过刺穿皮肤的插脚提供低于 1000 伏的电压和 1.5 毫安的电流。

较高的电压可以更好地使电流流过空气、衣服或肉体等障碍物，而幅度则可以衡量电流的强度。 因此，幅度决定了电击的物理影响，尽管电压影响实际输送电力的力。 G.L.O.V.E 的低电压意味着它只有直接涂抹在裸露皮肤上（或穿过浸湿的薄衣服）才能发挥作用。

虽然 G.L.O.V.E. 的设计是非致命性的。 确实有风险。 Compliant Technologies 的用户手册警告说，对一个人使用两个以上的 G.L.O.V.E 设备“可能会导致受伤或死亡”，并建议使用时间不要超过 15 秒。 它还警告不要使用 G.L.O.V.E. 针对弱势群体，如小孩或老人，或抓住人的头部、面部、喉咙、胸部或腹股沟。

可混搭光速

“我们认为，Compliant Technologies 的 CD3 技术是有史以来引入公共服务的最安全、最人性化、常识性、缓和升级的技术，”Compliant Technologies 的网站称。

Mashable 联系了 Compliant Technologies，但该公司拒绝进一步置评。

国土安全部发言人在发给 Mashable 的一份声明中表示，ICE 官员“在降级策略方面接受过严格训练”，并且他们会免除有关使用武力的定期持续培训。

国土安全部发言人表示：“ICE 正在不断评估我们现场官员的需求，以确保他们拥有必要的工具和设备，以安全逮捕并将犯罪的非法外国人驱逐出我国。” “每项决定都经过仔细考虑和适当审查，以确保 ICE 使用的任何技术都符合所有适用的执法政策和标准。”

然而，人权倡导者批评了向 ICE 特工推出 G.L.O.V.E。 ICE 因其特工使用武力而受到广泛关注，许多选民认为这种行为过度。

美国公民自由联盟 (ACLU) 平等部门政府事务主任诺林·沙阿 (Naureen Shah) 在给 Mashable 的一份声明中表示：“ICE 背叛了公众的信仰，目前不能相信它会在美国街头使用武力，更不用说使用未经测试的技术来对付他们认为构成威胁的任何人。”

多个美国机构已经在使用 G.L.O.V.E

图片来源：合规技术

ICE 并不是第一个使用 G.L.O.V.E. 的美国政府机构，G.L.O.V.E. 自 2018 年以来一直存在。 Compliant Technologies 的独家经销商 APB Consulting Solutions 声称，超过 700 个美国当地执法机构使用 CD3 技术，并且它是该国最大的此类设备经销商。

据报道，密苏里州开普吉拉多警察局在 2022 年了解到 G.L.O.V.E 后开始使用该设备，而路易斯维尔地铁惩教局是当年使用该设备的肯塔基州约 50 个机构之一。 德克萨斯州哈里斯县治安官办公室制定了使用 G.L.O.V.E. 的政策，密苏里州约翰逊县治安官办公室去年分享了一段警员培训使用 G.L.O.V.E. 的视频，Compliant Technologies 在 7 月宣布赢得了与北卡罗来纳州治安官协会的合同。

肯塔基州布利特县拘留中心此前曾使用过 G.L.O.V.E. 同样，但在 2023 年停止，因为一名员工被发现在对戴着手铐和脚镣的囚犯使用时过度用力。

更新：2026 年 8 月 14 日上午 10:20 AEST 本文已根据 DHS 和 ACLU 的评论进行了更新。
